newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, bellies end with limit gains.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, bellies end with limit gains.

text.p: CME lean hog and pork belly futures closed with limit gains in most contracts after Friday's USDA hog report showed producers did not aggressively expand herds this past quarter as had been expected, traders said.

At the close, traders estimated about 1,200 unfilled limit-bid buy orders remained in the August hogs, 850 in the October and 400 in the December. About 300 July pork belly bids and 500 August remained at the close.

Traders said the CME July and August hogs should trade Tuesday because the report's most bullish aspects supported the deferred contracts. That included a smaller-than-expected pig crop and breeding herd, both of which would support hog prices next fall.
"I saw the report as being most bullish for the October and December contracts," said Doug Harper, senior livestock analyst with Brock Associates.
Harper said environmental and social challenges in several leading hog producing states appear to have discouraged producers from enlarging herds and adding hog barns.
"I think both those numbers were shocking," said Dave Butterfield, commodity broker with Rand Finanical Services. "We were dialing in a bearish report (before Friday) and it just shocked everybody."

He was referring to the June 1 hog herd at 102 percent of a year ago and breeding herd at 101 percent. The breeding number was lower than all estimates in a Reuters survey, while the hog herd was at the low end of estimates.

Deferred hogs drew support from the report, while buying in July hogs was motivated by higher cash hog prices at Midwest markets, Butterfield said. CME July closed at premium to the average lean hog cash price, which some traders said should limit gains Tuesday in that contract.

Pork bellies closed with limit gains also in reaction to the USDA hog report, plus higher cash prices last week. USDA reported cash bellies, 12 to 14 lbs, were quoted at $88.00 per cwt, up $3.00 from Thursday.
CME hogs closed up 2.00 to 1.250 cents with July up 1.850 at 84.675 and August up the limit at 81.950.
Pork bellies were up the 3.00 cent limit in all contracts with July at 85.225 and August at 85.075.
